rows.what the ink shows: The short cancelled group has an s-shaped bend followed by a short upright with a separate dot; the cancellation thickens its lower strokes.
A tall initial l is followed by the small raised apostrophe and the joined rounded op group; the p descender remains below the cancellation and a terminal dot is separate.
A tall rounded initial stroke survives, but the following low letters are covered by a thick black cancellation; an independent a bowl cannot be separated.
The cancelled word retains a small initial hump, a long joined baseline and a hooked final stroke; the intervening bodies are hidden by the dense horizontal overstroke.

The second word has a looped d, closed o, low n and open terminal c. The first retains a large initial R-like bowl and a tall medial stroke, but the crossing hides the repeated p bodies and much of the ending.

The cancellation leaves an initial t-like upright, an oblique and upright group in the middle, and a later tall stem; most low bodies and the final letters merge with the continuous strike, preventing a secure three-word reading.
The pencilled word has an initial closed a, paired short r humps, another rounded a, then n and a descending g before the reduced er ending.

The crossed first line shows mettre followed by a tall l and small e. On the next line, parentheses enclose a tall left stem and a right h-shaped curved foot, followed by a dot and the distinct hooked 2; the central group is Th., not a four-stroke hash.

The underlined phrase begins with a large U followed by low ne. The next word shows two descending p strokes with rounded intervening o forms and a late crossed t, followed by a reduced connected ion ending; no separate abbreviation stop is visible.

The underlined heading retains a thin initial T/h-like skeleton and a final hooked numeral-like remnant, but a broad dark wave covers most of the word and the numeral top. The full title cannot be securely distinguished.

A straight cancellation covers the middle height of both words. Short low strokes, an isolated upright and a descender survive, but the internal letters and the exact abbreviation ending are not securely recoverable.

An initial upright with a lower hook and a later short cross-stem remain visible. The heavy horizontal and oblique cancellation conceals the intervening rounded letters and the ending, so toute remains uncertain.
The deleted word has a large looped d ascender followed by a small a-like bowl; the low joined n/s ending extends to the right beneath the single strike.

The slanted pencil note begins with an open capital C and shows the crossed t and accented ascending strokes in Caractérisation. The second line has the descending p, crossed t and final tall l of spectrale.
After the radical, the final rounded capital E has a clear left curve and rightward arms. The preceding glyph is covered by a dense dark blot, so the membership sign remains uncertain.

The upper deleted attempt contains a distinct tall h with a rightward shoulder. The strokes before it and the low letters after it are crossed by thick bars and a looping cancellation, leaving que and soit uncertain.

The continuation is overlaid by several heavy horizontal strokes and curved cancellation lines. Only disconnected loops, uprights and short low fragments remain; they do not separate into a secure sequence of words.

The opening q has a closed head and long descender, followed by the low ue; the next tall l and the final taller t remain visible across the cancellation. The middle joins are partly covered by the deletion strokes.

A rounded opening with a descending stroke and several short upright remnants survive before the rho. Two thick cancellation lines cover the connecting letters, preventing a defensible recovery of the two words.
The letter has a looped head with a descending stem; a separate short i and its dot sit lower to the right. The same loop-and-descender form occurs in the boxed sum below.

A tall l-like ascender and p-like descenders survive, but the cancellation covers enough letter bodies that the complete three-word sequence cannot be certified. The two enclosing parentheses are visible; the interior crossbar and short vertical remnants do not securely distinguish i from +.
Below the cancellation are the loop and final rising stroke of et, then the tall l and low joined ors of alors. Their upper portions are crossed out.

The compact parenthesized abbreviation has a small elevated 2. The nearby tall h is attached to the deleted line above: its ascender crosses that cancellation and its bowl stands above the live summand baseline; there is no separate baseline h after the square.

The long deletion leaves several descenders, low linked strokes and a tall final stem before the radical. It obscures the bodies of the opening words and much of propres, so the complete proposed phrase cannot be confirmed from surviving ink.
Immediately after Tr a curved left edge and a lower curved right remnant enclose heavily hatched ink. A u-shaped interior cannot be separated securely from the crossing strokes.
